why: FactionLeadersRecruitment DIVERGENCE: the card installs no saint pop-up handlers, so a prayer calls whatever saint_fn the previous card left; run from a start state no card installed them in, the original calls 0000:0000. The C# uses the standard saint rating.

CityLordsReward DIVERGENCE: the search for a saint nobody in the party knows (R089+0x0C5C) never ends when the party knows all 0x88 saints (the original hangs; the oracle stops at its instruction budget); the C# offers the boons with saint 0.
BattleStandIn (R045 188B:01E4) DIVERGENCE: the original goes to screen 0, whose table entry points into data (the game would crash); the C# goes back to the card before.

SneakingThroughTheHall DIVERGENCE: the original never calls card_load (it keeps the previous card's picture until the engine redraws); the C# shows the card at once. The oracle loads the card's own texts first, so everything after the C#'s show is compared.

Card 0x62 is the end of the game: the main loop (root 03A1:000A) stops when a card returns 0x62 and never runs this table entry; run directly, the original loads "$NoGo00.msg.msg", which does not exist, and its catalog code jumps into data.

CityWallSallyPort BUG/DIVERGENCE: the force-the-door chance reads the Strength of member number <highest Strength value> (DS:8DFC used as an index): the original reads memory past the party table, the C# an empty member (0). Every run whose hint or action uses that chance differs.
Card 0x0C is the overland map (R030 1462, the travel screen): it is ported as DarklandsGame.Travel, not as a card script, and its input is the map's, which the card policy does not drive.

VillageGraveyard UNCERTAIN: the hint handlers return a struct res they never fill in (only msg_buf gets "Success is assured."): the chance and member are stack leftovers (-558 and 2 here; the display shows the text for a negative chance); the C# says the text for the whole party.

BeforeTheCityWalls DIVERGENCE: examining the walls at night shows block 9, which $CityE00.msg does not have: the original prints the bytes after the last block, the C# an empty text.

Card 0xC2 ("$Forei03") has no message file in MSGFILES: the original's msg_load (R043 150B) takes the size of an entry catalog_find did not find and file_load_far runs off into memory outside the loaded code; the C# finds no texts and shows empty blocks. No other card script sets next_card to 0xC2.

Inventory.KeepEach DIVERGENCE: when every roll of keep_items_pct fails the original removes one stack more than the pack holds and leaves the item count at -1 (the next item added is lost); the C# pack ends empty (count 0). The record's other bytes are compared.

EmptyPrisonCell DIVERGENCE: the original draws block 0 as an option list (card_options) and returns at once, with no menu (the oracle records texts and menus as they are read); the C# shows the block as a text and waits. Everything else is compared.

CollectorsCommission runs on the quest event saved_card names; the oracle's start state has none (saved_card 0, no event in slot 0): the original reads the type byte of the unused record events[0] points to (a value no case has: default text 0), the C# an absent event (type 0, text 1). Without its quest the card cannot be compared.

Card 0x119 ($MeetH01) UNCERTAIN: its registration (R114 18D3:08B0) sets the saint pop-up handlers but not the item ones (DS:EB0A), so a potion chosen in the pop-up calls an earlier card's handler; the oracle starts with none (a null pointer: the original jumps to 0000:0000). The C# uses the default pop-up hint.

CityLeavingDirection DIVERGENCE: no line changes next_card, so the original offers the menu again for ever (its loop runs while next_card is 0x0C); the C# ends the card after one choice, with the same next card. The first menu and choice are compared.

why: Tester fault (forced handler calls): the original calls a far pointer 0000:0000, a handler slot nothing installed: opt_fn[k] of a line the card's text has no line for (its reset left it null), the hint of such a line, or the item_fn / saint_fn of a pop-up slot the card never fills (card_items / card_saints[k] = -1). The menu offers only the text's lines and the pop-up box lists only filled slots, so the game never makes that call; the C# goes on with its "screwed up." default or the line's pop-up handler. Everything up to the call is compared.

end: stops execution outside the loaded code at 00000
why: Tester fault, as the entry above: the original's trace agrees up to its call through a null handler slot (a line or pop-up slot the card never offers), the C# then ends the run its own way.

Oracle limit: line 0 (recruit) opens the inn's party roster (R038+0x0000), whose key loop (R038+0x02F8) waits for input the card oracle does not give; the oracle stops at its instruction budget there. The C# stubs the roster screen (CardContext.PartyRosterScreen) and returns to the menu. Here the line is also greyed (the party is full).

Docks, unlisted lines 10..19 (forced; the text has 8 lines, the init R051+0x2E4E enables them with its "screwed up." default): the switch has no case (R051+0x20D1), so the original goes round its loop again (R051+0x1F69), which lets an hour pass first (R051+0x201D); the C#'s CardMenu re-offers the menu without the outer round's hour. Unreachable: no lines 10..19 are ever offered.

Monastery, unlisted lines 10..19 (forced; the text has 9 lines and the init R057+0x1C46 points their handlers at the "screwed up." default R057+0x1C68): the switch has no case, so the original goes round its loop again and draws block 5 (the visit of the last twelve hours is now noted); the C#'s CardMenu re-offers block 0 without the outer round. Unreachable: no lines 10..19 are ever offered.

TatzelwurmPack, potion pop-up slots 2 and 3 (forced): their handlers R112+0x1438 / R112+0x143A are empty, so the throw takes the registers' leftovers as its chance and misses; the C# rates every slot with the potion hint. The card fills only two item slots (R112+0x12BE), so the box never lists slots 2 and 3.

GiantSpiderNest, potion pop-up slots 2 and 3 (forced): their handlers R112+0x253C / R112+0x253E are empty (the throw takes the registers' leftovers as its chance), the C# rates every slot with the potion hint. The card fills only two item slots (R112+0x23DE), so the box never lists slots 2 and 3.

Tester fault: the emulator itself raised on the original's side (hand_run.py records the exception as the trace line 'error ...' and the end 'error'; seen as a host access violation, gone on a rerun of the same job). Nothing of the original's run is recorded, so there is nothing to compare.

HuntsmanAtTheCamp: the card is reached only from the camp, whose discovery (R036, CampStay.SpendDay) sets saved_card (DS:E7D8) to the first guard or -1; it names that member ($ChosenOneName = party[saved_card]). A saved game's start state holds another saved_card (a card number), so the original reads a character record past the party (another member's text, or code: it stops), the C# an empty name. Not a state the card runs from in play.
